grammar.title: Imperative for instructions
grammar.explanation: El imperativo se usa para dar instrucciones directas. En inglés, se forma con el verbo base sin 'to'. A diferencia del español, no cambia según la persona: es igual para tú, usted, ustedes. Para hacer negativo, se usa 'Don't' + verbo base.
grammar.rule: Use the base form of the verb to give direct instructions or commands.
grammar.spanishTrap: Colombian speakers often add the subject pronoun ('You take your luggage') when giving instructions, but in English imperatives the subject is omitted ('Take your luggage').

examples.en: Take your luggage to the check-in counter.
examples.es: Lleva tu equipaje al mostrador de registro.

examples.en: Be sure to turn off your phone when the plane takes off.
examples.es: Asegúrate de apagar tu teléfono cuando el avión despegue.

commonErrors.wrong: You show your boarding pass to the agent.
commonErrors.correct: Show your boarding pass to the agent.
commonErrors.why: Imperatives don't use the subject pronoun 'you' before the verb.
Imperatives use the base form without 'to'.

grammar.title: Modal verb 'can' for possibility and ability
grammar.explanation: El modal 'can' expresa habilidad o posibilidad. A diferencia del español que usa diferentes formas (puedo, puedes, puede), 'can' nunca cambia. Se usa con el verbo base (sin 'to'). El negativo es 'can't' o 'cannot'.
grammar.rule: Use 'can' to express possibility or ability. It does not change form and is always followed by the base verb without 'to'.
grammar.spanishTrap: Spanish speakers often add 'to' after 'can' because Spanish uses 'poder + infinitivo', but in English it's 'can + base verb' (can go, NOT can to go).

examples.en: You can't risk being late for your business meeting.
examples.es: No puedes arriesgarte a llegar tarde a tu reunión de negocios.

examples.en: We can rebook you on the next flight.
examples.es: Podemos volver a reservarte en el próximo vuelo.

commonErrors.wrong: You can to board the plane now.
commonErrors.correct: You can board the plane now.
commonErrors.why: After 'can', use the base form without 'to'.

commonErrors.wrong: The offer can includes a hotel stay.
commonErrors.correct: The offer can include a hotel stay.
commonErrors.why: 'Can' is followed by the base verb without '-s' or '-es'.

grammar.title: Present simple for general truths and routines
grammar.explanation: El presente simple se usa para verdades generales, hábitos y situaciones permanentes. En tercera persona singular (he, she, it) se agrega -s o -es al verbo. A diferencia del español, el inglés siempre necesita el sujeto explícito (no podemos omitirlo).
grammar.rule: Use present simple for general truths, habits, and permanent situations. Add -s or -es to the verb for third person singular.
grammar.spanishTrap: Spanish allows omitting the subject pronoun ('Llega tarde' = He/she arrives late), but English always requires it ('He arrives late', NOT 'Arrives late').

examples.en: Most of the time, things go well.
examples.es: La mayor parte del tiempo, las cosas van bien.

examples.en: Airlines frequently increase the perks to convince people.
examples.es: Las aerolíneas aumentan frecuentemente los beneficios para convencer a la gente.

commonErrors.why: Third person singular needs -s on the verb.
Third person singular (it) requires -s on the verb.

grammar.title: Gerunds (-ing forms) as nouns
grammar.explanation: Los gerundios (verbo + -ing) funcionan como sustantivos en inglés. Se usan después de ciertas expresiones y verbos. A diferencia del español que usa infinitivos ('evitar llegar tarde'), el inglés usa gerundios después de verbos como 'risk', 'avoid', 'enjoy' ('risk being late').
grammar.rule: After certain verbs and prepositions, use the -ing form (gerund) to express an action as a noun.
grammar.spanishTrap: Spanish uses infinitives after many verbs ('No puedes arriesgar llegar tarde'), but English often requires gerunds ('You can't risk being late'). Also, after prepositions, Spanish uses infinitives but English uses gerunds.

examples.en: You can't risk being late for your business meeting.
examples.es: No puedes arriesgarte a llegar tarde a tu reunión de negocios.

examples.en: Volunteering to get off is probably out of the question.
examples.es: Ofrecerse voluntariamente para bajarse probablemente está fuera de cuestión.

commonErrors.wrong: I can't risk to be late.
commonErrors.why: After 'risk', use the gerund (-ing form), not the infinitive.

commonErrors.wrong: The airline is good at compensate passengers.
commonErrors.correct: The airline is good at compensating passengers.
commonErrors.why: After prepositions like 'at', use gerund (-ing form).

grammar.title: Adjectives describing offers and situations
grammar.explanation: Este tema enseña adjetivos para describir ofertas y situaciones de viaje. A diferencia del español, muchos de estos adjetivos se forman con prefijos negativos en inglés (un-, im-). Los adjetivos van antes del sustantivo o después de verbos como 'be' o 'seem'.
grammar.rule: Use adjectives like tempting, attractive, impossible, acceptable, awful to describe offers, ideas and experiences related to travel.
grammar.spanishTrap: En español se dice 'es difícil de rechazar', pero en inglés es 'it is hard to decline' (sin 'de'/'to' después del adjetivo cuando no hay verbo infinitivo).

examples.en: If an offer is tempting to you, it is hard to decline.
examples.es: Si una oferta es tentadora para ti, es difícil rechazarla.

examples.en: A perk is an attractive offer.
examples.es: Un beneficio es una oferta atractiva.

commonErrors.wrong: The offer is very tempting for decline.
commonErrors.correct: The offer is very tempting to decline.
commonErrors.why: 'Tempting' is followed by the infinitive with 'to', not a preposition.

commonErrors.wrong: An offer impossible is not acceptable.
commonErrors.correct: An impossible offer is not acceptable.
commonErrors.why: In English, adjectives go before the noun they describe.

grammar.title: Expressions with infinitives after adjectives
grammar.explanation: Cuando un adjetivo describe qué tan difícil o fácil es hacer algo, usamos la estructura: be + adjective + infinitivo con 'to'. En español usamos 'de' (difícil de hacer), pero en inglés NO usamos preposición entre el adjetivo y el infinitivo.
grammar.structure: It is + adjective + to + base verb
grammar.rule: After adjectives like hard, easy, impossible, tempting, use 'to + base verb' to show what action the adjective describes.
grammar.spanishTrap: Los colombianos suelen decir 'it is hard for decline' porque en español decimos 'es difícil de rechazar'. En inglés NO se usa preposición: 'hard to decline'.

examples.en: If an offer is tempting to you, it is hard to decline.
examples.es: Si una oferta es tentadora para ti, es difícil rechazarla.

examples.en: When an offer is too good to refuse, it's an excellent idea.
examples.es: Cuando una oferta es demasiado buena para rechazar, es una idea excelente.

commonErrors.wrong: It is impossible for accept the offer.
commonErrors.correct: It is impossible to accept the offer.
commonErrors.why: Use 'to + base verb' after adjectives, not 'for + base verb'.

commonErrors.wrong: The seat is easy to giving up.
commonErrors.correct: The seat is easy to give up.
commonErrors.why: After 'to', use the base form of the verb, not the -ing form.

grammar.title: Past simple tense in travel narratives
grammar.explanation: El pasado simple se usa para hablar de experiencias de viaje que ya terminaron. Los verbos irregulares cambian su forma (take → took, have → had, lose → lost). En español el pretérito tiene más formas, pero en inglés la forma del pasado simple es la misma para todas las personas.
grammar.rule: Use past simple to tell about completed travel experiences and transportation problems.
grammar.spanishTrap: En español decimos 'yo tomé' y 'él tomó' con formas diferentes del verbo. En inglés es la misma forma: 'I took' y 'he took'.

examples.en: I took a limo on my business trip.
examples.es: Tomé una limusina en mi viaje de negocios.

examples.en: We missed our train.
examples.es: Perdimos nuestro tren.

commonErrors.wrong: I take a ferry the last time.
commonErrors.correct: I took a ferry the last time.
commonErrors.why: Use past simple (took) when talking about completed past actions.
'Lose' is irregular; the past form is 'lost', not 'losed'.

grammar.title: Conditional sentences with 'if' (zero conditional)
grammar.explanation: Las oraciones con 'if' en el presente se usan para hablar de situaciones generales o hechos que siempre son ciertos. La estructura usa presente simple en ambas partes. A diferencia del subjuntivo en español, en inglés estas oraciones usan el indicativo (presente simple).
grammar.structure: If + subject + present simple, subject + present simple
grammar.rule: Use 'if + present simple' to describe general truths or situations that are always true, especially when explaining vocabulary or concepts.
grammar.spanishTrap: En español usamos subjuntivo después de 'si' en algunos casos (si fuera...), pero en el zero conditional inglés SIEMPRE usamos presente simple, nunca subjuntivo.

examples.en: If someone volunteers to get off the plane, she or he gets off.
examples.es: Si alguien se ofrece como voluntario para bajarse del avión, ella o él se baja.

examples.en: If an airline compensates you, it gives you a voucher.
examples.es: Si una aerolínea te compensa, te da un cupón.

commonErrors.wrong: If someone will volunteer, he gets off.
commonErrors.correct: If someone volunteers, he gets off.
commonErrors.why: In zero conditional, use present simple in both parts, not 'will'.

commonErrors.wrong: If an offer is tempting, it will be hard to decline.
commonErrors.correct: If an offer is tempting, it is hard to decline.
commonErrors.why: For general truths, use present simple in the result clause, not future.

grammar.title: 'Too' + adjective
grammar.explanation: En inglés, 'too' antes de un adjetivo significa 'demasiado' y expresa un exceso negativo. A diferencia del español donde 'demasiado' puede ser positivo o negativo, en inglés 'too' siempre implica algo malo o excesivo. Se coloca directamente antes del adjetivo.
grammar.rule: Use 'too' before an adjective to show excessive or negative degree.
grammar.spanishTrap: Los hispanohablantes pueden colocar 'too' después del adjetivo como en español ('caro demasiado'), pero en inglés siempre va antes.

examples.en: The shop is too small.

commonErrors.why: 'Too' meaning 'demasiado' must come before the adjective

grammar.title: Expressing preferences with 'like to wear'
grammar.explanation: En inglés, para expresar lo que te gusta vestir, usas 'I like to wear' + prenda de vestir. A diferencia del español donde dices 'me gusta usar/vestir', en inglés el sujeto es 'I' y el verbo es 'like', seguido del infinitivo 'to wear'. No necesitas el pronombre reflexivo 'me' como en español.
grammar.rule: Use 'like to wear' to express clothing preferences, followed by the clothing item and optionally the situation (at home, on a hot day, for a party).
grammar.spanishTrap: Los hispanohablantes tienden a traducir 'me gusta usar' literalmente, diciendo 'I like wear' sin el 'to'. En inglés, después de 'like' siempre debes usar 'to' + verbo en infinitivo.

examples.en: I like to wear a sweater over a shirt to keep warm on a cool day.
examples.es: Me gusta usar un suéter sobre una camisa para mantenerme abrigado en un día fresco.

examples.en: I like to wear an old sweatshirt and sweatpants at home.
examples.es: Me gusta usar una sudadera vieja y pantalones deportivos en casa.

commonErrors.wrong: I like wear a T-shirt at home.
commonErrors.correct: I like to wear a T-shirt at home.
commonErrors.why: After 'like', you must use 'to' before the verb.

commonErrors.wrong: I like to wear a shorts on a hot day.
commonErrors.correct: I like to wear shorts on a hot day.
commonErrors.why: Shorts is already plural, so we don't use 'a' before it.

grammar.title: Using 'or' to present alternatives
grammar.explanation: En inglés, 'or' se usa para presentar opciones o alternativas, igual que 'o' en español. La diferencia es que en inglés no se usa 'o...o' como a veces en español ('o esto o lo otro'), sino simplemente 'or'. Se coloca entre las dos opciones sin cambiar de forma.
grammar.rule: Use 'or' between two clothing items or choices to show alternatives or options.

examples.en: I like to wear a dress shirt or blouse with a pair of khakis or slacks.
examples.es: Me gusta usar una camisa de vestir o blusa con un par de pantalones caqui o pantalones.

examples.en: I like to wear a T-shirt and sweatpants at home, but not at a party.
examples.es: Me gusta usar una camiseta y pantalones deportivos en casa, pero no en una fiesta.

commonErrors.wrong: I like to wear a shirt and a sweater and a coat on a cool day.
commonErrors.correct: I like to wear a shirt or a sweater or a coat on a cool day.
commonErrors.why: When presenting options, use 'or' not 'and'.

commonErrors.wrong: I like to wear khakis slacks for a party.
commonErrors.correct: I like to wear khakis or slacks for a party.
commonErrors.why: You need 'or' to connect the two alternatives.

grammar.title: Using 'but not' to express contrast
grammar.explanation: En inglés, 'but not' se usa para hacer un contraste o excepción. Es como decir 'pero no' en español. Se usa cuando algo es cierto en una situación pero no en otra. La estructura es: [afirmación positiva], but not [situación/lugar donde no aplica].
grammar.rule: Use 'but not' to show a contrast between where you do wear something and where you don't wear it.

examples.en: I like to wear a T-shirt and sweatpants at home, but not at a party.
examples.es: Me gusta usar una camiseta y pantalones deportivos en casa, pero no en una fiesta.

examples.en: I like to wear an old sweatshirt at home, but not at a party.
examples.es: Me gusta usar una sudadera vieja en casa, pero no en una fiesta.

commonErrors.wrong: I like to wear jeans at home but at a party not.
commonErrors.correct: I like to wear jeans at home, but not at a party.
commonErrors.why: The word order should be 'but not' followed by the place or situation.

commonErrors.wrong: I like to wear shorts at home, but I not like to wear shorts at a party.
commonErrors.correct: I like to wear shorts at home, but not at a party.
commonErrors.why: Use the shorter form 'but not' instead of repeating the whole sentence.

grammar.title: Prepositional phrases for situations: at/on/for
grammar.explanation: En inglés, diferentes preposiciones se usan según la situación. 'At' se usa para lugares (at home, at a party), 'on' se usa para días específicos o tipos de días (on a hot day, on a cool day), y 'for' se usa para eventos o propósitos (for a party). A diferencia del español donde usarías 'en' para la mayoría de estos casos, el inglés distingue más.
grammar.rule: Use 'at' for places, 'on' for types of days, and 'for' for events or purposes when talking about when or where you wear clothing.
grammar.spanishTrap: Los hispanohablantes tienden a usar 'in' para todas las situaciones porque en español 'en' funciona para todo. En inglés debes distinguir: 'at home' (no 'in home'), 'on a hot day' (no 'in a hot day'), 'for a party' (no 'to a party' cuando hablas de ropa).

examples.en: I like to wear an old sweatshirt at home.
examples.es: Me gusta usar una sudadera vieja en casa.

examples.es: Me gusta usar shorts en un día caluroso.

commonErrors.correct: I like to wear a bathing suit on a hot day.

commonErrors.correct: I like to wear a nice suit for a party at a friend's home.
commonErrors.why: Use 'for' when talking about what you wear for an event.

grammar.title: Superlative Adjectives with 'in town'
grammar.explanation: En inglés, los adjetivos superlativos (the cheapest, the best, the biggest) se usan para comparar algo con todos los demás en un grupo. A diferencia del español donde decimos 'el más barato de la ciudad', en inglés usamos 'the cheapest in town'. Nota que 'best' y 'worst' son formas irregulares.
grammar.structure: the + superlative adjective + noun + in town/in the world/in the country
grammar.rule: Use superlative adjectives to compare one thing with all others in a group or place.
grammar.spanishTrap: Los hispanohablantes a menudo dicen 'the most cheap' en lugar de 'the cheapest', traduciendo literalmente 'el más barato'. Los adjetivos cortos (cheap, big, low) añaden -est, no 'most'.

examples.en: They've got the lowest prices in town.
examples.es: Tienen los precios más bajos del pueblo.

examples.en: This place has the biggest selection of brands in town.
examples.es: Este lugar tiene la selección más grande de marcas del pueblo.

commonErrors.wrong: They've got the most cheap prices in town.
commonErrors.correct: They've got the cheapest prices in town.
commonErrors.why: Short adjectives like 'cheap' form superlatives with -est, not 'most'.

commonErrors.wrong: This place has the bigger selection in town.
commonErrors.correct: This place has the biggest selection in town.
commonErrors.why: Use superlative form 'biggest' (not comparative 'bigger') when comparing with all others in a group.

grammar.title: Future with 'will' for Decisions
grammar.explanation: En inglés usamos 'will' + verbo base para decisiones tomadas en el momento de hablar. Es como el futuro simple español 'voy a' o 'haré'. Nota que después de 'will' el verbo SIEMPRE va en forma base (sin 'to', sin -s, sin -ing).
grammar.rule: Use 'will' + base form of verb to express decisions made at the moment of speaking.
grammar.spanishTrap: Los hispanohablantes añaden '-s' después de 'will' con 'he/she/it' (I'll takes) porque en español el verbo cambia. Pero después de 'will', el verbo NUNCA cambia: I'll take, he'll take, we'll take.

examples.en: I'll take these!
examples.es: ¡Me llevo estos!

examples.en: We'll keep shopping.
examples.es: Seguiremos comprando.

commonErrors.why: After 'will', always use the base form of the verb without -s.

commonErrors.wrong: The salesperson will holds them for you.
commonErrors.correct: The salesperson will hold them for you.
commonErrors.why: After 'will', use base form 'hold', not 'holds'.

grammar.title: Expressions with 'What a...!'
grammar.explanation: En inglés, 'What a + sustantivo!' expresa sorpresa o emoción fuerte. Es similar a '¡Qué...!' en español, pero en inglés SIEMPRE necesitas el artículo 'a' con sustantivos contables singulares. Con sustantivos plurales o incontables, se usa solo 'What' (sin 'a').
grammar.structure: What a + singular noun! / What + plural/uncountable noun!
grammar.rule: Use 'What a + noun!' to express surprise about something specific.
grammar.spanishTrap: Los hispanohablantes olvidan 'a' porque en español decimos solo '¡Qué ganga!' sin artículo. En inglés, con sustantivos contables singulares, 'a' es obligatorio: 'What a bargain!'

commonErrors.wrong: What bargain! These shoes are on sale.
commonErrors.correct: What a bargain! These shoes are on sale.
commonErrors.why: With singular countable nouns, you must include 'a' after 'What'.

commonErrors.wrong: What a best service in town!

grammar.title: Object Pronouns: Direct Object
grammar.explanation: En inglés, los pronombres de objeto directo reemplazan el sustantivo que recibe la acción del verbo. A diferencia del español donde 'lo/la' puede ir antes del verbo, en inglés SIEMPRE van después del verbo. Ejemplo: 'I want it' (Lo quiero), NO 'I it want'.
grammar.structure: Subject + verb + object pronoun (me, you, him, her, it, us, them)
grammar.rule: An object pronoun replaces a noun or a noun phrase when it functions as a direct object.
grammar.spanishTrap: Los colombianos tienden a colocar el pronombre antes del verbo como en español ('lo quiero'), pero en inglés debe ir después del verbo ('I want it').

examples.en: I want the belt. → I want it.
examples.es: Quiero el cinturón. → Lo quiero.

examples.en: She loves those sandals. → She loves them.
examples.es: A ella le encantan esas sandalias. → A ella le encantan.

commonErrors.why: Object pronouns come after the verb in English, not before.
'They' is a subject pronoun; use 'them' as the object pronoun.

grammar.title: Object Pronouns: Prepositional Phrase
grammar.explanation: En frases preposicionales (con 'to', 'for', etc.), el pronombre de objeto va después de la preposición. En español 'a ella' o 'para él', en inglés 'to her' o 'for him'. Los pronombres de objeto (me, you, him, her, us, them) se usan en estas posiciones, NO los pronombres de sujeto.
grammar.structure: Verb + (object) + preposition (to/for) + object pronoun (me, you, him, her, us, them)
grammar.rule: In a prepositional phrase, use object pronouns (me, you, him, her, it, us, them) after prepositions like to and for.
grammar.spanishTrap: Los colombianos pueden usar pronombres de sujeto después de preposiciones ('for she' en lugar de 'for her'), porque en español las formas pueden parecer similares.

examples.en: Did you give your credit card to the salesperson? → Did you give your credit card to her?
examples.es: ¿Le diste tu tarjeta de crédito al vendedor? → ¿Le diste tu tarjeta de crédito a ella?

examples.en: I'm buying a blue blazer for my husband. → I'm buying a blue blazer for him.
examples.es: Estoy comprando un blazer azul para mi esposo. → Estoy comprando un blazer azul para él.

commonErrors.why: Use object pronoun 'him' after the preposition 'for', not subject pronoun 'he'.

commonErrors.wrong: Did you give it to she?
commonErrors.correct: Did you give it to her?
commonErrors.why: Use object pronoun 'her' after the preposition 'to', not subject pronoun 'she'.

grammar.title: Direct Object Before Prepositional Phrase
grammar.explanation: Cuando una oración tiene tanto un objeto directo como una frase preposicional, el objeto directo viene primero. En español el orden puede variar, pero en inglés es fijo: verbo + objeto directo + preposición + objeto. Ejemplo: 'Did you give the scarf to your brother?' NO 'Did you give to your brother the scarf?'
grammar.structure: Subject + verb + direct object + prepositional phrase
grammar.rule: When a sentence has both a direct object and a prepositional phrase, the direct object comes first.
grammar.spanishTrap: En español el orden puede ser flexible ('Le di a mi hermano la bufanda' o 'Le di la bufanda a mi hermano'), pero en inglés el objeto directo siempre va antes de la frase preposicional.

examples.en: Did you give the scarf to your brother?
examples.es: ¿Le diste la bufanda a tu hermano?

examples.en: I'm buying a blue blazer for my husband.
examples.es: Estoy comprando un blazer azul para mi esposo.

commonErrors.wrong: Did you give to your brother the scarf?
commonErrors.correct: Did you give the scarf to your brother?
commonErrors.why: The direct object 'the scarf' must come before the prepositional phrase 'to your brother'.

commonErrors.wrong: I'm buying for my husband a blue blazer.
commonErrors.correct: I'm buying a blue blazer for my husband.
commonErrors.why: The direct object comes before the prepositional phrase.

grammar.title: Object pronouns (me, you, him, her, it, us, them)
grammar.explanation: Los pronombres objeto reemplazan al objeto de la oración (la persona o cosa que recibe la acción). En español usas 'me, te, lo/la, nos, los/las', pero en inglés las formas son diferentes: me, you, him/her/it, us, them. Siempre van después del verbo, no antes como en español.
grammar.structure: Subject + verb + object pronoun + (rest of sentence)
grammar.rule: Use object pronouns (me, you, him, her, it, us, them) to replace the person or thing receiving the action. They come after the verb.
grammar.spanishTrap: En español los pronombres de objeto van ANTES del verbo ('lo compro'), pero en inglés van DESPUÉS ('I buy it'). También, 'it' se usa para cosas y animales, no solo 'lo/la'.

examples.en: I'll take it in black.
examples.es: Me lo llevaré en negro.

examples.en: Can you help? I'd like these five items, but I want to keep shopping.
examples.es: ¿Puedes ayudar? Me gustan estos cinco artículos, pero quiero seguir comprando.

examples.en: I can hold for you.
examples.es: Puedo guardártelo.

examples.en: Are you giving your husband that tie?
examples.es: ¿Le estás dando esa corbata a tu esposo?

commonErrors.why: Object pronouns come after the verb in English, not before like in Spanish

commonErrors.correct: Can you give it to me?
commonErrors.why: You need to include the object pronoun 'it' before 'to me'

grammar.title: Modal verb 'should' for giving advice
grammar.explanation: Usamos 'should' para dar consejos o recomendaciones. Es similar a 'debería(s)' en español. Siempre va seguido del verbo en forma base (sin 'to'). Para el negativo, usamos 'shouldn't' (no 'don't should').
grammar.rule: Use 'should' + base verb to give advice. Use 'shouldn't' for negative advice.
grammar.spanishTrap: Después de 'should' el verbo va en forma base, sin 'to'. No digas 'should to buy' como podrías traducir 'debería comprar'. También, el negativo es 'shouldn't', no 'don't should'.

examples.en: You should definitely buy.
examples.es: Definitivamente deberías comprar.

examples.en: Actually, you shouldn't buy those.
examples.es: En realidad, no deberías comprar esos.

examples.en: Should I buy this short-sleeve shirt?
examples.es: ¿Debería comprar esta camisa de manga corta?

commonErrors.why: Don't use 'to' after 'should'
The negative of 'should' is 'shouldn't', not 'don't should'

grammar.title: Possessive adjectives (my, your, his, her, our, their)
grammar.explanation: Los adjetivos posesivos (my, your, his, her, its, our, their) indican de quién es algo. En inglés, el adjetivo posesivo NO cambia según el género o número del objeto poseído, como en español ('mi libro', 'mis libros' vs. 'my book', 'my books').
grammar.rule: Use possessive adjectives before nouns to show ownership. They don't change form based on what is owned.
grammar.spanishTrap: En inglés, el posesivo no cambia por el género ni el número de lo que se posee. 'My' es igual para 'mi libro' y 'mis libros'. También, 'his' es 'de él' y 'her' es 'de ella', no cambian por el objeto.

examples.es: Es su cumpleaños.

examples.en: Are you giving your husband that tie?
examples.es: ¿Le estás dando esa corbata a tu esposo?

examples.en: It is for my sister-in-law.
examples.es: Es para mi cuñada.

commonErrors.wrong: I'm buying a gift for she.
commonErrors.correct: I'm buying a gift for her.
commonErrors.why: After prepositions like 'for', use object pronouns (her), not subject pronouns (she)
'His' is the possessive adjective; 'him' is an object pronoun

grammar.title: Present continuous for actions happening now
grammar.explanation: El presente continuo (am/is/are + verbo-ing) describe acciones que están ocurriendo en este momento. Es similar al gerundio en español ('estoy comprando'). Se forma con el verbo 'to be' más el verbo principal terminado en -ing.
grammar.rule: Use present continuous (am/is/are + verb-ing) to describe actions happening right now.
grammar.spanishTrap: En inglés necesitas el verbo 'to be' antes del gerundio. No puedes decir 'I buying', tiene que ser 'I am buying'. También, algunos verbos como 'want' y 'need' normalmente NO se usan en continuo en inglés.

examples.en: I'm buying a gift for Mom.
examples.es: Estoy comprando un regalo para mamá.

examples.en: Are you giving your husband that tie?
examples.es: ¿Le estás dando esa corbata a tu esposo?

examples.en: I'm giving a nice dress shirt, too.
examples.es: También estoy dando una linda camisa de vestir.

commonErrors.why: You must include 'am/is/are' before the -ing verb
'Want' is not normally used in continuous form

grammar.title: Polite requests with 'Can you...?'
grammar.explanation: Usamos 'Can you...?' para hacer solicitudes educadas. Es como '¿Puedes...?' en español. La estructura es simple: Can you + verbo base. Es menos formal que 'Could you...?' pero muy común en tiendas y conversaciones cotidianas.
grammar.rule: Use 'Can you...?' to make polite requests. Follow it with the base form of the verb.
grammar.spanishTrap: Después de 'Can you' va el verbo en forma base, sin 'to'. No digas 'Can you to help'. También, 'Can you' es para pedir a otros; 'Can I' es para pedir permiso para ti mismo.

grammar.title: Superlative Adjectives
grammar.explanation: Los superlativos comparan más de dos personas, lugares, cosas o ideas. En español usamos 'el/la/los/las más' + adjetivo. En inglés, para adjetivos cortos agregamos '-est' (cheap → the cheapest), y para adjetivos largos usamos 'the most' o 'the least' antes del adjetivo (comfortable → the most comfortable). Siempre usamos 'the' con superlativos en inglés.
grammar.structure: the + adjective + est / the most/least + adjective
grammar.rule: Use superlative adjectives to compare more than two people, places, things, or ideas. Use 'the' before a superlative adjective.
grammar.spanishTrap: En español decimos 'el más barato' o 'la más bonita' pero en inglés el artículo siempre es 'the', no cambia por género: 'the cheapest' para masculino y femenino. Además, nunca olvides 'the' — en inglés es obligatorio con superlativos.

examples.en: Which of these men's coats is the cheapest?
examples.es: ¿Cuál de estos abrigos de hombre es el más barato?

examples.en: Jake's Shoes has the best prices in town.
examples.es: Jake's Shoes tiene los mejores precios del pueblo.

examples.en: This sweater is the least expensive.
examples.es: Este suéter es el menos caro.

commonErrors.correct: This is the most expensive store.
commonErrors.why: Always use 'the' before superlative adjectives

commonErrors.correct: She has the most beautiful dress.
commonErrors.why: Long adjectives (3+ syllables) use 'the most' not '-est'

grammar.title: Formation of Superlative Adjectives with -est
grammar.explanation: Para adjetivos cortos (1-2 sílabas), formamos el superlativo agregando '-est': cheap → the cheapest, great → the greatest, nice → the nicest, cute → the cutest. Para adjetivos que terminan en consonante + vocal + consonante, duplicamos la última consonante: big → the biggest, hot → the hottest.
grammar.rule: Add -est to short adjectives. If an adjective ends in consonant + vowel + consonant, double the last consonant before adding -est.
grammar.spanishTrap: No traduzcas literalmente 'el más'. En inglés, para adjetivos cortos solo agregamos '-est', no usamos 'more' nunca: 'the cheapest' NO 'the most cheap'.

examples.en: cheap → the cheapest
examples.es: barato → el más barato

examples.en: nice → the nicest
examples.es: agradable → el más agradable

examples.en: big → the biggest
examples.es: grande → el más grande

commonErrors.wrong: This is the most cheap store.
commonErrors.why: Short adjectives use -est, not 'the most'
Double the final consonant before -est when adjective ends in consonant-vowel-consonant

grammar.title: Formation of Superlative Adjectives with the most/the least
grammar.explanation: Para adjetivos largos (2+ sílabas que no terminan en -y), usamos 'the most' o 'the least' antes del adjetivo sin cambiar el adjetivo: expensive → the most expensive, comfortable → the most comfortable, attractive → the most attractive. 'The least' significa 'el menos' y es el opuesto de 'the most'.
grammar.rule: If the adjective has two or more syllables and doesn't end in -y, use 'the most' or 'the least' before the adjective.
grammar.spanishTrap: No agregues '-est' a adjetivos largos. En español decimos 'el más cómodo', en inglés 'the most comfortable' NO 'the comfortablest'.

examples.en: This sweater is the least expensive.
examples.es: Este suéter es el menos caro.

examples.en: Those shoes are the most comfortable.
examples.es: Esos zapatos son los más cómodos.

examples.en: The most popular stores are on Smith Street.

commonErrors.correct: This is the most expensive blender.
commonErrors.why: Long adjectives use 'the most', not -est

commonErrors.correct: That restaurant is the most popular.
commonErrors.why: Always include 'the' before 'most' in superlatives

grammar.title: Irregular Superlatives: good and bad
grammar.explanation: Los adjetivos 'good' y 'bad' tienen formas irregulares de superlativo. 'Good' se convierte en 'the best' (el mejor), y 'bad' se convierte en 'the worst' (el peor). Igual que en español (bueno → el mejor, malo → el peor), no siguen las reglas normales.
grammar.structure: good → the best / bad → the worst
grammar.rule: The superlative of 'good' is 'the best'. The superlative of 'bad' is 'the worst'.
grammar.spanishTrap: No digas 'the goodest' o 'the most good'. La forma correcta es 'the best', igual que en español no dices 'el más bueno' sino 'el mejor'.

examples.en: Jake's Shoes has the best prices in town.
examples.es: Jake's Shoes tiene los mejores precios del pueblo.

examples.en: good → the best
examples.es: bueno → el mejor

examples.en: bad → the worst
examples.es: malo → el peor

commonErrors.why: 'Good' has irregular superlative 'the best'

commonErrors.why: 'Bad' has irregular superlative 'the worst'

grammar.title: Asking for Recommendations
grammar.explanation: Para pedir recomendaciones usamos 'Do you recommend...?' o 'Can you recommend...?' seguido del lugar o cosa. También podemos preguntar '¿Cuál es el más...?' usando 'What's the most/least + adjective + noun?' En español usamos '¿Recomiendas...?' o '¿Puedes recomendar...?'
grammar.structure: Do you recommend + place/thing? / Can you recommend + place/thing? / What's the most/least + adjective + noun?
grammar.rule: Use 'Do you recommend' or 'Can you recommend' followed by a place or thing to ask for shopping advice.
grammar.spanishTrap: Después de 'recommend' usamos el nombre directo, no 'to go to': 'Do you recommend Gloria's Jeans?' NO 'Do you recommend to go to Gloria's Jeans?'

examples.en: Do you recommend Gloria's Jeans?

examples.en: Can you recommend a store that has bargains on kitchen equipment?

examples.es: ¿Cuál es la marca más popular de zapatos para correr ahora?

commonErrors.wrong: Do you recommend to go to that mall?
commonErrors.why: Use direct object after 'recommend', not 'to go to'
Always use 'the' with superlatives

grammar.title: Giving Recommendations with Superlatives
grammar.explanation: Para dar recomendaciones combinamos el lugar/cosa con un superlativo para explicar por qué es bueno: 'Try [place]. It's the + superlativo + lugar/cosa.' También usamos 'Absolutely!' o 'Definitely!' para enfatizar una recomendación positiva.
grammar.structure: Try + place. It's the + superlative + noun / Absolutely/Definitely + place/thing + verb + superlative
grammar.rule: Give recommendations by naming a place and explaining why using a superlative adjective.
grammar.spanishTrap: En inglés ponemos el adjetivo antes del sustantivo: 'the best Japanese restaurant' NO 'the Japanese restaurant best' como a veces estructuramos en español.

examples.en: Try the Park Plaza. It's the newest mall in town.
examples.es: Prueba el Park Plaza. Es el centro comercial más nuevo del pueblo.

examples.en: Absolutely! They're the most comfortable jeans we sell.
examples.es: ¡Por supuesto! Son los jeans más cómodos que vendemos.

examples.en: Sid's Sushi is the best Japanese restaurant in that neighborhood.
examples.es: Sid's Sushi es el mejor restaurante japonés en ese vecindario.

commonErrors.wrong: Try that store. Is the cheap most.
commonErrors.correct: Try that store. It's the cheapest.
commonErrors.why: Superlative adjective needs 'the' before it and comes after 'It's'

commonErrors.wrong: Definitely! They're jeans the most comfortable.
commonErrors.correct: Definitely! They're the most comfortable jeans.
commonErrors.why: Adjective comes before noun in English

grammar.title: Using 'That depends' to give conditional responses
grammar.explanation: Esta expresión se usa cuando tu respuesta depende de más información. En español puedes decir 'depende' solo, pero en inglés siempre necesitas el sujeto 'that'. Es común en conversaciones cuando alguien te hace una pregunta pero necesitas saber más detalles antes de responder.
grammar.rule: Use 'That depends' when your answer changes based on more information, then ask a question to get that information
grammar.spanishTrap: Colombian speakers often say just 'Depends' (translating 'Depende' directly), but in English you must say 'That depends' or 'It depends' — the subject is required

examples.en: That depends. What are you looking for?
examples.es: Eso depende. ¿Qué estás buscando?

examples.en: Where's the best place in town to buy footwear? That depends.
examples.es: ¿Dónde está el mejor lugar en la ciudad para comprar calzado? Eso depende.

commonErrors.wrong: Depends. What are you looking for?
commonErrors.correct: That depends. What are you looking for?
commonErrors.why: In English, 'depends' needs a subject. Use 'That depends' or 'It depends'
'Depends' needs an -s because 'that' is third person singular

grammar.title: Superlatives with 'the most' + adjective
grammar.explanation: Para decir que algo es número uno en su categoría, usamos 'the most' + adjetivo largo (convenient, expensive) o 'the' + adjetivo corto + '-est' (largest, best). A diferencia del español donde 'más' va antes del adjetivo en todos los casos, en inglés depende del tamaño de la palabra.
grammar.structure: the most + adjective OR the + adjective + -est
grammar.rule: Use 'the most' with long adjectives (2+ syllables) and 'the -est' with short adjectives to show something is number one
grammar.spanishTrap: Spanish uses 'el más' for all adjectives, but English uses 'the most' only for long adjectives. Short adjectives use 'the -est' instead

examples.en: It's probably the most convenient.
examples.es: Probablemente es el más conveniente.

examples.en: Tom's Outdoor Store has the largest selection and the best bargains.

grammar.title: Asking for recommendations with 'Where's the best place'
grammar.explanation: Esta estructura se usa para pedir recomendaciones sobre lugares. En inglés, a diferencia del español, usamos 'where is' (no 'where are') porque 'place' es singular, aunque estés preguntando sobre varios lugares posibles. La respuesta típicamente usa superlativos.
grammar.rule: Use 'Where's the best place' + location phrase + 'to' + verb to ask for recommendations about places
grammar.spanishTrap: In Spanish you might say '¿Dónde hay...?' or '¿Dónde están...?' but in English use 'Where is' (singular) because you're asking about 'the place' (one recommendation)

examples.en: Where's the best place in town to buy footwear?

commonErrors.correct: Where's the best place to buy sandals?
commonErrors.why: After 'place' use 'to' + verb, not 'for' + verb

commonErrors.correct: Where's the best place to buy sweaters?
commonErrors.why: 'Place' is singular, so use 'is' not 'are'

grammar.title: Expressing preferences with 'I'd like' + noun
grammar.explanation: Usamos 'I'd like' (I would like) para expresar lo que queremos de forma educada. Es más formal que 'I want'. En español es como 'me gustaría'. Después va un sustantivo (something, a store) o un verbo en infinitivo con 'to'.
grammar.rule: Use 'I'd like' + noun to politely express what you want or prefer
grammar.spanishTrap: Don't confuse 'I'd like' with 'I like'. 'I'd like' = me gustaría (want), 'I like' = me gusta (enjoy). After 'I'd like', if you use a verb, you need 'to'

commonErrors.correct: I'd like something near the subway station.
commonErrors.why: 'I like' means you enjoy it. Use 'I'd like' (would like) to say you want it

grammar.title: Prepositions with floors and locations: on vs in
grammar.explanation: En inglés, usamos 'on' para hablar de pisos (on the first floor, on the second floor). A diferencia del español donde usamos 'en' para todo, en inglés 'in' se usa para áreas dentro de un espacio (in the front, in the back, in the basement). Nota: 'on' para pisos numerados, 'in' para secciones dentro del edificio.
grammar.structure: on + the + floor number / in + the + location area
grammar.rule: Use 'on' with floor numbers and 'in' with location areas like front, back, and basement.
grammar.spanishTrap: Spanish speakers say 'en el primer piso' for everything, but English requires 'on the first floor' (not 'in the first floor') for numbered floors.

examples.en: The men's department is on the third floor.

commonErrors.why: Use 'in' with 'basement', not 'on'.

grammar.title: Imperative for giving directions: Take the + noun
grammar.explanation: Para dar direcciones en inglés, usamos el imperativo (la forma base del verbo sin sujeto). La estructura es 'Take the' + medio de transporte o escaleras. En español decimos 'tome', pero en inglés no necesitamos pronombre de sujeto. Es directo y simple.
grammar.structure: Take + the + escalator/stairs/elevator + to + the + floor
grammar.rule: Use the base form of the verb 'take' followed by 'the' and the noun (escalator, stairs, elevator) to give directions.
grammar.spanishTrap: Spanish speakers may add 'you' because Spanish uses 'usted tome', but English imperative has no subject pronoun: 'Take the stairs' (not 'You take the stairs').

examples.en: Take the escalator to the third floor.

commonErrors.wrong: You take the stairs to the second floor.

commonErrors.why: Imperatives in English don't use a subject pronoun.

commonErrors.wrong: Takes the escalator to the first floor.
commonErrors.correct: Take the escalator to the first floor.
commonErrors.why: Use the base form 'take', not 'takes', for imperatives.

grammar.title: Phrasal verbs for movement: go up / go down
grammar.explanation: Los phrasal verbs 'go up' y 'go down' indican movimiento vertical. 'Go up' significa subir (hacia arriba) y 'go down' significa bajar (hacia abajo). A diferencia del español donde usamos verbos diferentes ('subir' y 'bajar'), en inglés usamos el mismo verbo 'go' con partículas diferentes. También se usan 'upstairs' (arriba) y 'downstairs' (abajo) como adverbios de lugar.
grammar.structure: Go up / Go down + the + escalator/stairs
grammar.rule: Use 'go up' for moving to a higher floor and 'go down' for moving to a lower floor.
grammar.spanishTrap: Spanish speakers may translate literally 'subir' as 'up' only, but in English you need the verb 'go' before 'up' or 'down'.

examples.en: Go up the escalator.
examples.es: Suba la escalera mecánica.

examples.en: Go down the stairs.
examples.es: Baje las escaleras.

commonErrors.wrong: Up the stairs to the second floor.
commonErrors.correct: Go up the stairs to the second floor.
commonErrors.why: You need the verb 'go' before 'up'.

commonErrors.correct: Go down to the first floor.
commonErrors.why: 'Go up' and 'downstairs' contradict each other; use 'go down' for moving to a lower floor.

grammar.title: Prepositions of location: in, on, at (for places in buildings)
grammar.explanation: En inglés, usamos 'on' para pisos específicos (on the second floor), 'in' para áreas generales (in the basement, in the store), y 'at' para puntos específicos (at the information desk). A diferencia del español donde usamos 'en' para casi todas estas situaciones, el inglés distingue entre superficie (on), interior (in), y punto específico (at).
grammar.rule: Use 'on' with floor numbers, 'in' with general areas like basement or departments, 'at' with specific points like desks or counters.
grammar.spanishTrap: Los hispanohablantes tienden a usar solo 'in' para todas las ubicaciones porque en español 'en' funciona para todos los contextos. Deben recordar que el inglés usa 'on' para superficies y pisos específicos.

grammar.title: Present continuous for current actions: I'm looking for
grammar.explanation: Usamos el presente continuo (am/is/are + verbo-ing) para hablar de acciones que están ocurriendo ahora o en el momento presente. En español se puede decir 'busco' o 'estoy buscando', pero en inglés en contextos de compras es más natural usar el presente continuo 'I'm looking for' para indicar tu búsqueda actual en la tienda.
grammar.rule: Use present continuous (am/is/are + verb-ing) to describe what someone is currently doing or searching for right now.
grammar.spanishTrap: Los hispanohablantes a veces usan presente simple cuando deberían usar presente continuo en contextos de compras, diciendo 'I look for' en lugar de 'I'm looking for', porque en español ambas formas son aceptables.

examples.es: Estoy buscando pantalonetas de correr.

examples.es: Disculpe. Estoy buscando pantalonetas de correr.

commonErrors.why: In shopping contexts, use present continuous to express what you're currently searching for
After am/is/are, use the -ing form of the verb, not the base form

grammar.title: Imperative for giving directions: Take the escalator
grammar.explanation: El imperativo en inglés se forma con el verbo base sin sujeto. Se usa para dar instrucciones o direcciones. A diferencia del español donde el imperativo cambia según 'tú/usted' (toma/tome), en inglés solo hay una forma que funciona para todas las personas. Es común y educado al dar direcciones.
grammar.rule: Use the base form of the verb (no subject) to give directions or instructions.
grammar.spanishTrap: Los hispanohablantes pueden agregar 'you' antes del verbo porque en español a veces decimos 'tú tomas' para énfasis, pero en inglés el imperativo nunca lleva sujeto.

Use the base form of the verb, not the third person singular form

grammar.title: Modal verb 'can' for ability and possibility
grammar.explanation: El modal 'can' se usa para expresar habilidad o posibilidad. Siempre va seguido del verbo en forma base (sin 'to'). En español se traduce como 'poder' (puedo, puede, pueden), pero a diferencia del español donde el verbo cambia según la persona, 'can' nunca cambia de forma.
grammar.rule: Use 'can' followed by the base form of the verb (no 'to') to express ability or offer help.
grammar.spanishTrap: Los hispanohablantes pueden agregar 'to' después de 'can' (can to hold) porque en español usamos 'poder + infinitivo', pero en inglés los modales van directamente seguidos del verbo base sin 'to'.

a2_4.content:
Hi! I'm Mari, your English tutor for **Family Relationships and Extended Family**.

I can see you've had trouble with *relatives* — let's work on those.

Write anything in English and I'll help you improve.
My sister is taller than me

Perfect sentence! Your sister must be tall.

Do you look alike, or are you very different?
My sister is taller than me

You already told me that! 

Does your sister live with you, or does she live somewhere else?

✏️ **"She live"** → **"She lives"** — third person singular needs -s.

Got it! Does she live far away, or pretty close to your house?

Today we're practicing **family relationships** — talking about relatives using comparative adjectives, present simple, and family vocabulary.

Who in your family do you get along with the most?
With my brother because he's funnier than me.

✏️ **"funnier than me"** → **"funnier than I am"** — but informally "than me" is widely accepted too!

Nice! How often do you two get together or hang out?

texts.title: Daily speaking training
texts.body:
Hi! My name is Dev, and I want to talk about my English learning app.
I made this app with help from an AI called Claude. This app is special because it is connected to my English book from American Schoolway.
I take photos of the pages from my book, and I upload them to the app. Then the app creates flashcards, exercises, grammar lessons, and speaking tests — all based on my book!
This is very helpful because I study exactly what my teacher teaches in class. Everything in the app is from my book.
For example, I can study new words with flashcards. I can do grammar exercises and practice speaking like a real exam.
My English is not perfect, but I practice every day with this app. And every day I get a little better.
Learning a new language is not easy. But if you work hard and practice every day, you can do it. Don't stop. Keep going!
Thank you for watching. See you next time!"

texts.title: U6 · pág 61
texts.body:
1. "In this photo, I don't think it's OK to use your phone at the table. When you eat with family or friends, you should talk to them, not look at a screen. It's a little rude."

2. "In this situation, it's not OK to text during a movie. The light from the phone bothers other people, and you're not really watching the movie."

3. "In this picture, texting while driving is very dangerous. You can't watch the road and your phone at the same time. It can cause an accident."

4. "In this photo, I think it's OK to listen to music while riding a bike, but you have to be careful. You still need to hear cars around you."

5. "In this situation, I don't think it's a good idea to use your phone while crossing the street. You need to watch for cars—it's safer to wait until you're on the other side."

texts.title: U6 · pág 62 - 63
texts.body: I have a laptop, a smart TV, wireless earbuds, and a printer. I use my laptop every day for my business, but right now, I have a problem with it. It's broken. It won't turn on. Actually, it's not obsolete — it's a fairly new laptop — but something is defective inside it. For starters, I lost some important work files because of this. Seriously, it's driving me crazy! I don't have a tablet, headphones, or speakers, and I don't really want them — my earbuds are enough for me. I'd like to have a desktop computer, a virtual assistant, a copier, a video camera, a fitness tracker, and a digital camera. Right now, though, I really need to fix or replace my laptop first, because I use it for everything in my business.

texts.title: U6 · pág 64 - 65
texts.body:
I have a dishwasher, a blender, a washing machine, a vacuum cleaner, and a hair dryer at home. Right now, I'm using my blender to make a smoothie — it's really top notch, and I use it almost every day. My washing machine is a little old, though. Actually, I'm washing some clothes right now, and it's very noisy. I don't have a food processor, a rice cooker, a juicer, or a dryer. I don't really need a food processor or a juicer, but I'm planning to buy a rice cooker next month — it would make cooking easier at home.
Actually, I'm shopping online right now. I'm looking for a new laptop — a MacBook, because mine is broken. It's very popular, and I hear it's top notch. It's convenient because it's fast and portable. But it's also a bit pricey — MacBooks are expensive. Still, I think it's worth it. It lasts for years, and the quality is excellent. I'm probably buying one this weekend.

texts.title: U6 · pág 66 - 67
texts.body:
I always take pictures with my phone. I love taking photos of nature, animals, and beautiful things that catch my attention during the day. I sometimes upload photos to social media, especially when I find something really beautiful. I usually make videos too — short videos of nature or animals I find interesting. But I hardly ever make photocopies, because I don't really need to for my business.
Actually, something is wrong right now. I'm trying to upload some photos, but my laptop isn't working. It's broken — it won't turn on. It's not obsolete; it's a fairly new laptop, but it's a piece of junk right now. It's driving me crazy, because I use it for everything in my business. For starters, I lost some important files. I'm probably taking it to a technician tomorrow, so I can fix it or buy a new one.

texts.title: U6 · pág 68 - 69
texts.body:
On a typical day, I use my smart phone to text, check email, post to social media, and sometimes play games. I sometimes check my phone first thing in the morning when I wake up, and I sometimes check it before I go to sleep too. I mostly use my phone when I'm bored — I usually stream movies or get information — but I'm trying to do other things instead, because I don't want it to become a dependence.
Actually, I think my phone usage is decreasing. I've realized that spending too much time on social media takes away time I could use to study English. So now I'm trying to use my phone less and focus more on my studies. I don't think I'm addicted, but I know it's easy for a habit to become a dependence if you're not careful.

instead.translation: en lugar de, en vez de

translation: En un día típico, uso mi celular para enviar mensajes, revisar el correo, publicar en redes sociales, y a veces jugar juegos.
A veces reviso mi celular apenas me despierto en la mañana, y a veces también lo reviso antes de dormir.

Mayormente uso mi celular cuando estoy aburrido — usualmente veo películas en streaming o busco información — pero estoy tratando de hacer otras cosas en su lugar, porque no quiero que se convierta en una dependencia.
De hecho, creo que mi uso del celular está disminuyendo.
Me he dado cuenta de que pasar demasiado tiempo en redes sociales me quita tiempo que podría usar para estudiar inglés.
Así que ahora estoy tratando de usar menos el celular y enfocarme más en mis estudios.
No creo que esté adicto, pero sé que es fácil que un hábito se convierta en una dependencia si no tienes cuidado.

texts.title: U6 · pág 70 - 71
texts.body:
*"I usually use a power strip at home, because I have a lot of devices to charge — my phone, my laptop, and my wireless earbuds. Sometimes I forget my charger when I travel, which is a problem, because then I can't charge my phone or turn it on when the battery dies. I think it would be a good idea to always pack an extra charger and an adapter, just in case.
If I stayed in a hotel and something wasn't working, it would be really annoying. For example, if the outlet was broken or the wi-fi wasn't working, I'd probably call the front desk. If the air-conditioner wouldn't turn on, or the toilet was clogged, I'd say, "Seriously? That's ridiculous!" I think traveling with technology can be stressful sometimes, because you always depend on power and a good connection.

texts.title: U5 · pág 49
texts.body:
Hi, I'm Divier. Today I want to talk about Eating in Restaurants, page 49 of my book.
When I go to a restaurant, I'm usually in the mood for grilled food. I love meat, and I always prefer it grilled or roasted instead of fried. I'm not a big fan of seafood, but I really like a good sandwich too. It depends on my mood — sometimes I want something heavy, like steak, and sometimes I just want something light and quick.
texts.trans:
Hola, soy Divier. Hoy quiero hablar de Eating in Restaurants, página 49 de mi libro.
Cuando voy a un restaurante, usualmente estoy en ánimo de comida a la parrilla. Me encanta la carne, y siempre la prefiero a la parrilla o asada en vez de frita. No soy muy fan de los mariscos, pero también me gusta mucho un buen sándwich. Depende de mi ánimo — a veces quiero algo pesado, como un bistec, y a veces solo quiero algo ligero y rápido.

texts.title: U5 · pág 50 - 51
texts.body:
Hi, I'm Divier. Today I want to talk about pages 50 and 51 of my book.
In my country, we have great dishes for every part of a meal. For an appetizer, I'd choose empanadas. For a salad, I'd choose an avocado salad. For an entrée, or main course, I'd choose bandeja paisa. For dessert, I'd choose arequipe. And for a beverage, I'd choose mango juice.
When I go to a restaurant, I'm usually starving, so I always look at the menu carefully to see if there's anything good for me. When I order meat, I always ask for it well done — I don't like it rare or medium. If I don't understand something on the menu, I say "Excuse me" and ask the server questions. At the end of the meal, we'll take the check, and I always ask if the tip is included, so I know how much to pay.
texts.trans:
ola, soy Divier. Hoy quiero hablar de las páginas 50 y 51 de mi libro.
En mi país, tenemos platos excelentes para cada parte de una comida. Para un aperitivo, elegiría empanadas. Para una ensalada, elegiría ensalada de aguacate. Para un plato principal, elegiría bandeja paisa. Para el postre, elegiría arequipe. Y para una bebida, elegiría jugo de mango.
Cuando voy a un restaurante, usualmente estoy muerto de hambre (starving), así que siempre miro el menú con cuidado para ver si hay algo bueno para mí. Cuando pido carne, siempre la pido bien cocida (well done) — no me gusta término medio o roja. Si no entiendo algo del menú, digo "Excuse me" y le hago preguntas al mesero. Al final de la comida, pedimos la cuenta (we'll take the check), y siempre pregunto si la propina está incluida, para saber cuánto pagar.

paisa.translation: persona de la región antioqueña de Colombia (Antioquia, Caldas, Risaralda, Quindío); también se refiere a su cultura y acento característico

arequipe.translation: dulce de leche (caramelo de leche espeso y cremoso típico de Colombia)

so.translation: tan, así, entonces, por lo tanto

server.translation: servidor/mesero (persona que sirve en restaurante) o servidor (computadora)

texts.title: U5 · pág 52 - 53
texts.body:
Hi, I'm Divier. Today I want to talk about ordering from a menu, pages 52 and 53 of my book.
I love eating out on the weekends. When I get to a restaurant, I usually check the menu first. If there's soup on the menu, I always order the soup, because I love it. I also love pasta, so if there's a pasta dish, I'll have the pasta. For my main course, I'll start with an appetizer, like a salad or some bread. Then, I'll have the grilled chicken. It usually comes with rice or potatoes and a salad. I'd like the potatoes and the mixed green salad. To drink, I'd like some sparkling water — I don't really like soda. And if there's a nice dessert on the menu, I'll have the chocolate cake. It's my favorite.
texts.trans:
"Hola, soy Divier. Hoy quiero hablar de pedir en un menú, páginas 52 y 53 de mi libro.
Me encanta comer afuera los fines de semana. Cuando llego a un restaurante, usualmente reviso el menú primero. Si hay sopa en el menú, siempre pido la sopa, porque me encanta. También me encanta la pasta, así que si hay un plato de pasta, pediré la pasta. Para mi plato principal, empezaré con un aperitivo, como una ensalada o un poco de pan. Luego, pediré el pollo a la parrilla. Usualmente viene con arroz o papas y una ensalada. Quisiera las papas y la ensalada verde mixta. Para tomar, quisiera un poco de agua con gas — no me gusta mucho la gaseosa. Y si hay un buen postre en el menú, pediré el pastel de chocolate. Es mi favorito.

texts.title: U5 · pág 54 - 55
texts.body:
Hi, I'm Divier. Today I want to talk about ways to prepare food, pages 54 and 55 of my book.
I really like grilled and roasted food. I also like baked dishes, and sometimes I order something stewed when it's cold outside. But I don't like boiled vegetables — I think steamed or sautéed vegetables taste much better. When I go to a restaurant, I don't want any fried food, because it's usually too heavy. I'd like some grilled chicken instead, or something roasted.
If a friend tells me they don't like fried food, I always agree — I say "Me neither!" And if someone says they love grilled food, I say "Me too!" I think it's nice when people share the same taste in food."
texts.trans:
"Hola, soy Divier. Hoy quiero hablar de las formas de preparar comida, páginas 54 y 55 de mi libro.
Me gusta mucho la comida a la parrilla y asada. También me gustan los platos horneados, y a veces pido algo guisado cuando hace frío. Pero no me gustan las verduras hervidas — creo que las verduras al vapor o salteadas saben mucho mejor. Cuando voy a un restaurante, no quiero nada frito, porque usualmente es muy pesado. Prefiero un poco de pollo a la parrilla, o algo asado.
Si un amigo me dice que no le gusta la comida frita, siempre estoy de acuerdo — digo "¡A mí tampoco!" Y si alguien dice que le encanta la comida a la parrilla, digo "¡A mí también!" Creo que es lindo cuando la gente comparte el mismo gusto por la comida."

texts.title: U5 · pág 56 - 57
texts.body:
In this picture, I can see healthy foods like apples, broccoli, and other vegetables. I can also see junk food, like a hamburger and french fries. I think fruits and vegetables are healthy, and fried foods like french fries are unhealthy because they're too fatty.
Now I want to tell you about my eating habits. In the morning, I usually eat something light for breakfast, like eggs or fruit. For lunch, I try to eat a balanced meal, with some protein, rice, and vegetables. I don't eat a lot of salty snacks, and I try to avoid fried food during the week. But on the weekends, I sometimes eat something sweet, like cake or ice cream, because I think it's OK once in a while. I try to eat low-fat food most of the time, but I also believe you can enjoy a treat sometimes, as long as you don't do it every day.
texts.trans:
En esta imagen, puedo ver comidas saludables como manzanas, brócoli y otras verduras. También puedo ver comida chatarra, como una hamburguesa y papas fritas. Creo que las frutas y verduras son saludables, y las comidas fritas como las papas fritas son poco saludables porque tienen mucha grasa.
Ahora quiero contarles sobre mis hábitos alimenticios. En la mañana, usualmente como algo ligero de desayuno, como huevos o fruta. Para el almuerzo, trato de comer una comida balanceada, con algo de proteína, arroz y verduras. No como muchos snacks salados, y trato de evitar la comida frita entre semana. Pero los fines de semana, a veces como algo dulce, como pastel o helado, porque creo que está bien de vez en cuando. Trato de comer comida baja en grasa la mayor parte del tiempo, pero también creo que puedes darte un gusto de vez en cuando, siempre y cuando no lo hagas todos los días.

texts.title: U5 · pág 58 - 59
texts.body:
Hi, I'm Divier. Today I want to talk about food habits and tastes, pages 58 and 59 of my book.
I like eating out sometimes, especially on weekends. I prefer eating in restaurants, or going home and cooking, instead of buying food from a street vendor. I don't eat food from carts, stands, or food trucks very often, because I don't think it's always fresh or clean — vendors sometimes don't use the correct hygiene measures, and that can make people sick. Food trucks are trendy now, but I still prefer a real restaurant.
As for my tastes, I really like grilled and salty food more than sweet food. I'm not a big fan of very spicy dishes either. Actually, my favorite food is still my mom's food — I love it the most, and I usually eat it when I go home. For me, eating at home just feels safer and more comfortable than buying ready-to-eat food on the street."
texts.trans:
"Hola, soy Divier. Hoy quiero hablar de hábitos y gustos de comida, páginas 58 y 59 de mi libro.
Me gusta salir a comer a veces, especialmente los fines de semana. Prefiero comer en restaurantes, o llegar a casa y cocinar, en vez de comprarle a un vendedor callejero. No como comida de carritos, puestos o food trucks muy seguido, porque no creo que siempre esté fresca o limpia — a veces los vendedores no usan las medidas de higiene correctas, y eso puede enfermar a la gente. Los food trucks están de moda ahora, pero aún prefiero un restaurante de verdad.
En cuanto a mis gustos, me gusta más la comida a la parrilla y salada que la comida dulce. Tampoco soy muy fan de los platos muy picantes. De hecho, mi comida favorita sigue siendo la de mi mamá — es la que más amo, y usualmente la como cuando voy a casa. Para mí, comer en casa se siente más seguro y cómodo que comprar comida lista para comer en la calle."

texts.title: U7 · pág 73
texts.body: I like three kinds of vacations. First, I like exciting vacations, because I want to try new things. For example, I want to go to a big water park and ride the slides. Second, I like interesting vacations, because I like to visit new places and learn about the people and the history. But my favorite kind is relaxing vacations, and for me that means good food, good music, and time with my family. I don't want to stay in the hotel all day, so I always walk or swim too. My vacations are short because I have a small business, so I travel on weekends. I usually travel with my brother and his girlfriend's family, and a big group is more fun. So my perfect vacation is relaxing, but with my family and a little activity too.
texts.trans: Me gustan tres tipos de vacaciones. Primero, me gustan las vacaciones emocionantes, porque quiero probar cosas nuevas. Por ejemplo, quiero ir a un parque acuático grande y lanzarme por los toboganes. Segundo, me gustan las vacaciones interesantes, porque me gusta visitar lugares nuevos y aprender sobre la gente y la historia. Pero mi tipo favorito son las vacaciones relajantes, y para mí eso significa buena comida, buena música y tiempo con mi familia. No quiero quedarme en el hotel todo el día, así que siempre camino o nado también. Mis vacaciones son cortas porque tengo un negocio pequeño, así que viajo los fines de semana. Normalmente viajo con mi hermano y la familia de su novia, y un grupo grande es más divertido. Así que mis vacaciones perfectas son relajantes, pero con mi familia y un poco de actividad también.

wh.q: What kinds of vacations do you like?
wh.a: I like three kinds. I like exciting vacations because I want to try new things, and I also like interesting vacations. But my favorite kind is relaxing vacations with my family.

wh.q: Why are your vacations short?
wh.a: My vacations are short because I have a small business. I can't close it for one week, so I travel on weekends. For example, I go away on Saturday and I come back on Sunday.

wh.q: Who do you travel with?
wh.a: I travel with my brother and his girlfriend's family. We are a big group, so it is more fun. For example, we eat together and we talk a lot.

wh.q: What do you do on a relaxing vacation?
wh.a: First, I eat good food and I listen to music. Then I talk with my family because I don't see them every day. But I don't want to stay in the hotel all day, so I always walk or swim.

Así que mis vacaciones perfectas son relajantes, pero con mi familia y un poco de actividad también.

texts.title: U7 · pág 74 - 75
texts.body: My favorite vacation activities are taking a tour, visiting a museum, and learning about other cultures. In my opinion, taking a tour is interesting, because the guide explains the history of the place. I also like hanging out with friends, because for me a good vacation is good food, good music, and my family. But I don't like going sport fishing, because you wait for many hours and I get bored. My favorite kind is a family vacation, so one day I want to go snorkeling with my brothers. For example, sometimes I take a staycation: I stay home and I sleep late. It isn't exciting, but it's relaxing. Finally, my vacations are short because I have a small business, so I travel on weekends.
texts.trans: Mis actividades favoritas en vacaciones son hacer un tour, visitar un museo y aprender sobre otras culturas. En mi opinión, hacer un tour es interesante, porque el guía explica la historia del lugar. También me gusta pasar el rato con amigos, porque para mí unas buenas vacaciones son buena comida, buena música y mi familia. Pero no me gusta la pesca deportiva, porque esperas muchas horas y me aburro. Mi tipo favorito son las vacaciones familiares, así que algún día quiero hacer snorkel con mis hermanos. Por ejemplo, a veces hago un staycation: me quedo en casa y duermo hasta tarde. No es emocionante, pero es relajante. Finalmente, mis vacaciones son cortas porque tengo un negocio pequeño, así que viajo los fines de semana.

wh.q: What are your favorite vacation activities?
wh.a: My favorites are taking a tour, visiting a museum, and learning about other cultures. In my opinion, taking a tour is interesting, because you learn a lot in one day. I also like hanging out with friends and eating good food.

wh.q: Which activity do you not like?
wh.a: I don't like going sport fishing. You wait for many hours, so I get bored. But my family likes it, and I go with them sometimes.

wh.q: What kinds of vacations do you like?
wh.a: I like family vacations, because a big group is more fun. We eat together and we talk a lot. But sometimes I take a staycation at home, and that is relaxing too.

wh.q: Why are your vacations short?
wh.a: My vacations are short because I have a small business. I can't go away for one week, so I travel on weekends. For example, I leave on Saturday and I come back on Sunday.

texts.title: U7 · pág 76 - 77
texts.body: Three months ago I went to Melgar with my parents and my brothers. First, the drive was pretty long and kind of boring, but the road was quite scenic. Our hotel was very comfortable, and the pools were really nice, so we swam every day. Then we took a tour, and it was really interesting, because the guide was so friendly. After that, I was next to the pool and I fell asleep in the sun, so my back was really red. That night I wasn't comfortable, so I didn't sleep well. On Sunday the town was very hot, but the shops were quite cheap. Finally, the trip was pretty short, but it was so nice, because we were all together.
texts.trans: Hace tres meses fui a Melgar con mis papás y mis hermanos. Primero, el viaje en carro fue bastante largo y algo aburrido, pero la carretera era muy panorámica. Nuestro hotel era muy cómodo, y las piscinas estaban muy bonitas, así que nadamos todos los días. Luego hicimos un tour, y fue muy interesante, porque el guía era muy amable. Después, estaba al lado de la piscina y me quedé dormido al sol, así que mi espalda quedó muy roja. Esa noche no estaba cómodo, así que no dormí bien. El domingo el pueblo estaba muy caliente, pero las tiendas estaban bastante baratas. Finalmente, el viaje fue bastante corto, pero fue muy agradable, porque estuvimos todos juntos.

wh.a: I was in Melgar with my family. The hotel was very comfortable, and the pools were really nice. It was a short trip, but it was so much fun.

wh.q: How was the drive?
wh.a: The drive was pretty long and kind of boring. But the road was quite scenic, so I looked out the window. Finally, we arrived at night, and I was really tired.

wh.q: What happened next to the pool?
wh.a: I was next to the pool, and I fell asleep in the sun. My back was really red, so I wasn't comfortable that night. It was funny, but it wasn't the end of the world.

wh.q: Who were you with?
wh.a: I was with my parents and my brothers. We were a big group, so it was more fun. For example, we were all together at dinner, and we talked a lot.

texts.title: U7 · pág 78 - 79
texts.body: Three months ago I went to Melgar with my parents and my brothers. First, we bought round-trip tickets, because we wanted to come back on Sunday night. I got a window seat, but my brother wanted an aisle seat, so we changed. Then the bus left at six in the morning, and the trip took four hours. After that, we arrived at the hotel and we had lunch. I didn't take a tour on Saturday, because I was really tired, so I relaxed next to the pool. On Sunday we walked in the town and we bought some gifts. Finally, we came back at night, and it was so nice, because we were all together.
texts.trans: Hace tres meses fui a Melgar con mis papás y mis hermanos. Primero, compramos tiquetes de ida y vuelta, porque queríamos regresar el domingo en la noche. Me tocó una silla de ventana, pero mi hermano quería una de pasillo, así que cambiamos. Luego el bus salió a las seis de la mañana, y el viaje tomó cuatro horas. Después, llegamos al hotel y almorzamos. No hice el tour el sábado, porque estaba muy cansado, así que descansé al lado de la piscina. El domingo caminamos por el pueblo y compramos unos regalos. Finalmente, volvimos en la noche, y estuvo muy bueno, porque estábamos todos juntos.

wh.a: I went to Melgar with my parents and my brothers. We took a bus, and the trip took four hours. It was short, but it was really nice.

wh.a: I bought a round-trip ticket, because I wanted to come back on Sunday. I didn't buy a one-way ticket, so we had our seats for both days. For example, we left on Saturday and we came back on Sunday night.

wh.q: How long did the trip take?
wh.a: The trip took four hours. The bus left at six in the morning, so I slept a little. But I got a window seat, and the road was quite scenic.

wh.q: What did you do on Sunday?
wh.a: We walked in the town and we bought some gifts. After that, we had lunch together, because it was our last day. Finally, we came back home at night.

texts.title: U7 · pág 80 - 81
texts.body: Three months ago, in 2026, I went to Melgar with my parents and my brothers. It was a mixture of good and bad experiences. First, the bus had mechanical problems, so we arrived two hours late, and that drove me crazy. But the hotel was very comfortable, and the pools were really nice, so we relaxed every day. Then we visited the town and we walked in the market, because we wanted to buy some gifts. After that, I stayed in the sun too long, so my back was really red and I didn't sleep well that night. But it wasn't the end of the world, because my family was there and we talked and laughed all afternoon. Finally, we came back on Sunday night, and I really liked the trip.
texts.trans: Hace tres meses, en 2026, fui a Melgar con mis papás y mis hermanos. Fue una mezcla de experiencias buenas y malas. Primero, el bus tuvo problemas mecánicos, así que llegamos dos horas tarde, y eso me volvió loco. Pero el hotel era muy cómodo, y las piscinas estaban muy bonitas, así que descansamos todos los días. Luego visitamos el pueblo y caminamos por el mercado, porque queríamos comprar unos regalos. Después, me quedé mucho tiempo al sol, así que mi espalda quedó muy roja y no dormí bien esa noche. Pero no fue el fin del mundo, porque mi familia estaba ahí y hablamos y nos reímos toda la tarde. Finalmente, volvimos el domingo en la noche, y el viaje me gustó mucho.

wh.a: It was a mixture of good and bad experiences. The hotel was very comfortable, and the pools were really nice. But the bus had mechanical problems, so we arrived late.

wh.q: What was the bad experience?
wh.a: The bus had mechanical problems, and that drove me crazy. Also, I stayed in the sun too long, so my back was really red. But it wasn't the end of the world.

wh.q: What did you do in the town?
wh.a: We visited the town and we walked in the market. We wanted to buy some gifts for my family. After that, we had lunch together, because we were really hungry.

wh.q: When did you get back?
wh.a: We came back on Sunday night, three months ago. The trip was pretty short, but I really liked it. Finally, we arrived home very late.

texts.title: U7 · pág 82 - 83
texts.body: In February 2024, I flew to Cartagena with my family. First, we left home very early, but there was a lot of traffic in Bogotá, so we arrived at the airport late. I was really nervous, because I didn't want to miss the flight. But the line was fast, so I went through security and I got my boarding pass on time. After that, we ran to the departure lounge and an agent called our flight. Then the plane took off on time and it landed on time too. It wasn't bumpy, and they didn't lose my luggage, so we had no problems. Finally, Cartagena was very hot, but the trip was great, because we were all together.
texts.trans: En febrero de 2024, volé a Cartagena con mi familia. Primero, salimos de la casa muy temprano, pero había mucho trancón en Bogotá, así que llegamos tarde al aeropuerto. Yo estaba muy nervioso, porque no quería perder el vuelo. Pero la fila fue rápida, así que pasé por seguridad y me dieron mi pasabordo a tiempo. Después, corrimos a la sala de embarque y un agente llamó nuestro vuelo. Luego el avión despegó a tiempo y aterrizó a tiempo también. No estuvo movido, y no perdieron mi maleta, así que no tuvimos problemas. Finalmente, Cartagena estaba muy caliente, pero el viaje estuvo muy bueno, porque estábamos todos juntos.

wh.q: When did you fly to Cartagena?
wh.a: I flew to Cartagena in February 2024. I went with my family, and it was a short trip. But we really enjoyed it, because the city was beautiful.

wh.q: What happened before the flight?
wh.a: There was a lot of traffic in Bogotá, so we arrived at the airport late. I was really nervous, because I didn't want to miss the flight. But the line was fast, and we made it on time.

wh.q: Did you have any problems on the flight?
wh.a: No, I didn't. The plane took off on time and it landed on time. It wasn't bumpy, and they didn't lose my luggage.

wh.q: How was Cartagena?
wh.a: Cartagena was very hot, but the trip was great. We were all together, and that is the best part for me. Finally, I want to go back one day.

texts.title: U8 · pág 85
texts.body: That depends. Sometimes I buy my clothes in a department store at the mall, because I like to try them on before I pay. But they're too expensive at the mall, so I don't go very often. Other times I buy online, and that is easy because I can compare many shops on my phone. But sometimes the size is wrong, and then I have to send it back. I also buy in small shops near my house, because they are cheaper and I know the people there. For example, I bought a shirt in a small shop for my trip to Melgar. Finally, it depends on the money and the time, but I usually prefer the small shops.
texts.trans: Eso depende. A veces compro mi ropa en un almacén por departamentos en el centro comercial, porque me gusta medírmela antes de pagar. Pero es muy cara en el centro comercial, así que no voy muy seguido. Otras veces compro por internet, y eso es fácil porque puedo comparar muchas tiendas en mi celular. Pero a veces la talla no queda, y entonces me toca devolverla. También compro en tiendas pequeñas cerca de mi casa, porque son más baratas y conozco a la gente de ahí. Por ejemplo, compré una camisa en una tienda pequeña para mi viaje a Melgar. Finalmente, depende de la plata y del tiempo, pero normalmente prefiero las tiendas pequeñas.

wh.q: Where do you usually buy your clothes?
wh.a: That depends. Sometimes I go to a department store at the mall, but it's expensive, so I don't go very often. Other times I buy online, and I also buy in small shops near my house.

wh.q: Why do you like small shops?
wh.a: I like small shops because they are cheaper. I also know the people there, so it's more comfortable for me. For example, I bought a shirt there for my trip to Melgar.

wh.q: What is the problem with buying online?
wh.a: Sometimes the size is wrong, and then I have to send it back. But it is easy, because I can compare many shops on my phone. So I still buy online, but not every time.

wh.q: Do you go to the mall often?
wh.a: No, I don't. The clothes are too expensive at the mall, so I don't go very often. But I like to try them on before I pay, and that's the good part.
